'''Goryō Shrine''' (御霊神社, also pronounced *Goryō Jinja*, *Gorei Jinja*, or *Mitama Jinja*) is a type of {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} named after the concept of "Goryō" (御霊), meaning honored spirits or venerated souls.

The deities (saijin) and nature of these shrines vary, reflecting different aspects of {{ill|Goryō|en|Goryō|qid=Q3273210|lt=Goryō belief}}. Some Goryō Shrines were established to appease the spirits of specific individuals, particularly vengeful spirits (怨霊), believed to cause misfortune. Others enshrine five divine spirits (五霊, *Goryō*) as a collective or may honor ancestral spirits (*Mikage* or *Mitama*) under the title of "Goryō" (御霊).
